extracted.intended_audience: broadcast television licensees, prospective reverse-auction applicants, designated entities, and FCC staff administering auctions and gift acceptance
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and procedures governing participation in the FCC's broadcast television spectrum incentive (reverse) auction, reporting of designated-entity eligibility events, confidentiality and communications restrictions, and FCC rules for acceptance and disclosure of gifts to the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reportable eligibility events
rubrics_metrics.description: A designated entity must seek Commission approval for all reportable eligibility events. A reportable eligibility event is: (1) any spectrum lease (as defined in § 1.9003) or any other type of spectrum use agreement with one entity or on a cumulative basis that might cause a licensee to lose eligibility for installment payments, a set-aside license, or a bidding credit (or for a particular level of bidding credit) under § 1.2110 and applicable service-specific rules; (2) any other event that would lead to a change in the eligibility of a licensee for designated entity benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This defines what must be reported and requires Commission approval prior to or when such events occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application contents and document filing for eligibility events
rubrics_metrics.description: A designated entity filing an application pursuant to this section must list and summarize on the application all agreements and arrangements (including proposed agreements and arrangements) that give rise to or relate to a reportable eligibility event, include the parties (including affiliates, controlling interests, spectrum lessees, resellers and wholesalers) and dates, file a copy of each agreement with the application, and maintain at its facilities or with agents, for the term of the license, the lists, summaries, dates, and copies required to be provided to the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must provide complete lists/summaries and copies; retain records for license term; party identification must be comprehensive (affiliates, controlling interests, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application fees and treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: The application reporting the eligibility event will be treated as a transfer of control for purposes of determining the applicable application fees as set forth in § 1.1102.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should expect fee treatment consistent with transfer-of-control filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamlined approval procedures for eligibility-event applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility event applications will be placed on public notice once sufficiently complete; petitions to deny must comply with § 1.939 and be filed no later than 14 days after the Public Notice listing the application as accepted for filing; the Wireless Telecommunications Bureau will grant, deny, or remove the application from streamlined processing no later than 21 days after the Public Notice listing; grants will be reflected in Public Notice; if removed from streamlined processing, Bureau will issue Public Notice and within 90 days take action or provide public notice that an additional 90-day period is needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timelines are strict: 14-day window for petitions to deny, 21-day Bureau decision for streamlined matters, and specified 90-day review windows when removed from streamlined processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice and application content requirements (eligibility events)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications under this section will be placed on informational public notice on a weekly basis and must contain all information requested on the applicable form, any additional information and certifications required by the rules in this chapter, and any service-specific rules for which the application is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all form questions and rule-specific certifications are answered; expect weekly public notice placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing update obligation for designated entities
rubrics_metrics.description: The designated entity is required to update any change in a relationship that gave rise to a reportable eligibility event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuing duty to update Commission filings when relationships change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice of incentive-auction procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission shall provide public notice of any procedures necessary for the implementation of an incentive auction that are not otherwise provided for pursuant to the rules of this Subpart. The Commission may do so in one or more such public notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auction-implementation procedures not in the rules will be published by public notice; participants must monitor public notices for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spectrum usage rights relinquishment procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures pursuant to which a licensee may make an unconditional, irrevocable offer to relinquish spectrum usage rights in exchange for an incentive payment, including any terms the offer must include and procedures pursuant to which the Commission may accept such an offer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public notice will specify the required offer terms and acceptance procedures for relinquishing rights in the incentive auction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information required from a licensee for relinquishment
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for a licensee to provide identifying information and/or certifications the Commission may require from any licensee that seeks to relinquish spectrum usage rights, and procedures for a licensee relinquishing rights to provide any financial information the Commission may require to facilitate disbursement of any incentive payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect requirements for identification, certifications, and financial information; specifics will be provided by public notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defined terms for broadcast television reverse auction (§ 1.2200)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions of terms used throughout §§ 1.2200–1.2209, including 'broadcast television licensee' (full‑power or low‑power Class A accorded primary status), 'channel sharee' (licensee that relinquishes rights to share a channel), 'channel sharer' (licensee sharing its channel), 'channel sharing bid', 'forward auction', 'reverse auction', 'reverse auction bid' (license relinquishment, UHF-to-VHF, high‑VHF-to‑low‑VHF, channel sharing bid), 'NCE station', 'Spectrum Act', and 'UHF-to‑VHF bid'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions set the meanings of key terms used in the auction rules and eligibility/certification requirements; applicants must use these definitions when completing applications and certifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice of competitive bidding design options
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to conducting competitive bidding in the reverse auction, public notice shall be provided of the detailed procedures that may be used to implement auction design options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design choices (collecting bids, assigning winning bids, payments, etc.) will be described in advance by public notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for collecting bids
rubrics_metrics.description: Public notice may establish procedures for collecting bids including: single- or multi‑round collection; collecting bids for multiple reverse auction bid options; bids that specify a price or indicate demand at a specified price; contingent bids; multi‑stage collection and transitions between stages; and rules for whether, when, and how bids may be modified during the auction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bid formats, rounds, contingency rules, and modification rules will be specified by public notice; bidders must follow the announced collection procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for assigning winning bids
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures may take into account factors in addition to bid amount (e.g., population coverage, geographic contour), evaluate technical feasibility (including use of mathematical computer optimization software such as integer programming or sequential ranking routines), combine optimization algorithms with other decision routines, and incorporate public interest considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Winning-bid determination may use multi-factor analyses and computational optimization; bidders should not assume simple highest-price wins in all cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for determining payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures to determine the amount of any incentive payments made to winning bidders consistent with other auction design choices. The amount of proceeds shared with a broadcast television licensee will not be less than the amount of the licensee's winning bid in the reverse auction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment calculations will be specified in public notice; guaranteed that shared proceeds will be at least the licensee's winning bid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice of competitive bidding procedures and required details
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed competitive bidding procedures shall be established by public notice prior to the commencement of the reverse auction, including sequencing of reverse and forward auctions, reserve prices (disclosed or undisclosed), opening bids and bid increments (maximum/minimum), and activity rules requiring a minimum amount of bidding activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auction mechanics (sequence, reserves, opening bids, increments, activity requirements) will be announced and govern conduct during the auction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Binding obligation of bids
rubrics_metrics.description: A bid is an unconditional, irrevocable offer by the bidder to fulfill the terms of the bid. The Commission accepts the offer by identifying the bid as winning. A bidder has a binding obligation to fulfill the terms of a winning bid. A winning bidder will relinquish spectrum usage rights pursuant to the terms of any winning bid by the deadline set forth in § 73.3700(b)(4) of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bids are legally binding when identified as winning; bidders must be prepared to comply with relinquishment terms and deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stopping procedures for the auction
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures may be established regarding when bidding will stop for a round, a stage, or an entire auction, in order to terminate the auction within a reasonable time and in accordance with public interest considerations and the goals, statutory requirements, rules, and procedures for the auction, including any reserve price(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stopping rules will be defined to balance efficiency, public interest, and statutory goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auction delay, suspension, or cancellation authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The auction may be delayed, suspended, or cancelled by public notice or during the auction in the event of natural disaster, technical obstacle, network disruption, auction security breach or unlawful bidding activity, administrative or weather necessity, or any other reason affecting the fair and efficient conduct of competitive bidding. The Commission may resume bidding from current or prior rounds or cancel the auction entirely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission retains broad discretion to interrupt or terminate auctions for reasons affecting fairness or feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application filing method and applicant identity requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications to participate must be filed electronically. The applicant identified must be the broadcast television licensee that would relinquish spectrum usage rights if it becomes a winning bidder; for a channel sharing bid the applicant will be the proposed channel sharee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the licensee (or proposed channel sharee for sharing bids) may be the applicant; electronic filing is mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information and certifications required in application to participate
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may be required to provide identifying information (names, addresses, corporate officer info, partner/trustee details), applicant ownership information per § 1.2112(a), identity of authorized bidders, for each license station the station identity and channel, whether full‑power or Class A (with certification of Class A compliance), NCE status, types of reverse auction bids to be submitted, whether license is subject to pending revocation/cancellation/downgrade proceedings (with acknowledgment of escrow of proceeds if so), and any additional information required to assess offered spectrum usage rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications contain extensive identity, ownership, and station‑specific certifications; accuracy is critical and many items are certified under penalty of perjury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional application items for license relinquishment bids
rubrics_metrics.description: For each license for which the applicant intends to submit a license relinquishment bid, an applicant must state whether it intends to enter a channel sharing agreement if it becomes a winning bidder, whether it will control another broadcast station if it terminates operations (with acknowledgments regarding pending renewals/enforcement or escrow of proceeds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relinquishment bidders must disclose future operational/control intentions and accept escrow or other conditions where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application requirements for channel sharing bids
rubrics_metrics.description: For each license for which the applicant intends to submit a channel sharing bid: identify the channel sharer and television channel agreed to share; provide required information regarding the channel sharing agreement, including a copy of the executed agreement; certify under penalty of perjury that the agreement is consistent with Commission rules and policies and accept risks of implementation; certify operation from shared facilities will not change Designated Market Area; certify community of license coverage requirements or provide alternative allotment priority justification; certify that arrangement will not violate multiple ownership rules based on facts at time of submission; and the channel sharer must provide parallel certifications under penalty of perjury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Channel sharing bids require an executed agreement and multiple specific certifications under penalty of perjury addressing technical feasibility, market area, community coverage, and ownership rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: National security and authority certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Certification under penalty of perjury that the applicant and disclosed persons are not barred for reasons of national security from bidding/participating, that the applicant assumes sole responsibility for investigating/evaluating technical and marketplace factors affecting its bids, that bids submitted are irrevocable, binding offers, and that the individual submitting the application is authorized to do so (with evidence of authority if not an officer/director/controlling interest).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes national security bar, investigatory responsibility, irrevocability of bids, and signer authority—each certified under penalty of perjury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application processing rules, amendability, and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Timely submitted applications will be reviewed for completeness; untimely applications will not be reviewed. Any application missing required certifications is unacceptable for filing, cannot be corrected after the filing deadline, and will be dismissed with prejudice. Applicants will be given a limited opportunity to cure specified defects and resubmit corrected applications during a resubmission period; after that period, only minor amendments are permitted (major amendments such as ownership changes, required certification changes, or addition/removal of licenses are not allowed). Applicants failing to correct defects timely will have applications dismissed with no resubmission opportunity. Applicants have a continuing obligation to amend pending applications to maintain accuracy and completeness within five business days after becoming aware of the need to amend or five business days after the reportable event occurs, whichever is later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines and cure opportunities are tight; major amendments prohibited after deadlines; continuing obligation to update within five business days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to qualified and non‑qualified applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Each applicant will be notified as to whether it is qualified or not qualified to participate in the reverse auction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should expect affirmative notification of qualification status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on certain communications about bids and strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning on the deadline for submitting applications to participate in the reverse auction and until results are announced by public notice, all full power and Class A broadcast television licensees are prohibited from communicating directly or indirectly any incentive auction applicant's bids or bidding strategies to any other full power or Class A broadcast television licensee or to any forward auction applicant, except as specified in (b)(2) exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict no‑sharing rule during the bidding period to prevent collusion; applies to controlling interests, officers, directors, and governing board members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to communications prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibition does not apply to communications between licensees that share a common controlling interest, director, officer, or governing board member as of the application deadline; communications between a forward auction applicant and a licensee if a controlling interest/director/officer/10%+ owner of the forward applicant is also such a party in the licensee as of relevant deadlines; and communications regarding reverse auction applicants' (but not forward auction applicants') bids and strategies between parties to a channel sharing agreement executed prior to the application deadline and disclosed on a reverse auction application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specified ownership/control overlaps and pre‑existing channel sharing agreements permit certain communications; parties should verify whether they meet exception criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to report potentially prohibited communications
rubrics_metrics.description: A party that makes or receives a communication prohibited under paragraph (b) shall report such communication in writing immediately, and in any case no later than five business days after the communication occurs. The reporting obligation continues until the report has been made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt written reporting (within five business days) is required for any prohibited communication; ongoing duty until report is filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for reporting prohibited communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports shall be filed as directed in public notices detailing procedures for bidding; if no public notice provides direction, the party shall report in writing to the Chief of the Auctions and Spectrum Access Division, Wireless Telecommunications Bureau, by the most expeditious means available (including electronic transmission such as email).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the reporting route in the applicable public notice or use the Bureau's Auctions and Spectrum Access Division contact if none is specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violations and sanctions for prohibited communications
rubrics_metrics.description: A party found to have violated the antitrust laws or the Commission's rules in connection with participation in the competitive bidding process may be subject to forfeiture of its winning bid incentive payment, revocation of its licenses where applicable, prohibition from participating in future auctions, and other applicable sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences are severe—potential forfeiture of payments, license revocation, and exclusion from future auctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of Commission‑held data
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will take all reasonable steps necessary to protect all Confidential Broadcaster Information for all reverse auction applicants from the time the licensee applies to participate until the reassignments and reallocations become effective or until two years after public notice that the reverse auction is complete and no such reassignments/reallocations will become effective. If reassignments/reallocations become effective, the Commission will continue to protect Confidential Broadcaster Information pertaining to unsuccessful reverse auction bids and unsuccessful applications until two years after the effective date. The Commission may disclose Confidential Broadcaster Information if required by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidentiality protections apply for specified periods; disclosure may occur if legally required (e.g., court order).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Confidential Broadcaster Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential Broadcaster Information includes Commission‑held data of a broadcast television licensee participating in the reverse auction such as the name of the applicant licensee, the licensee's channel number, call sign, facility identification number, network affiliation, and any other information that may reasonably be withheld to protect the identity of the licensee, as determined by the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain identifying information is explicitly listed as confidential; Commission has discretion to withhold other data to protect identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two competing participants required for agreements sharing proceeds
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may not enter into an agreement for a licensee to relinquish spectrum usage rights in exchange for a share of the proceeds from the related forward auction assigning new spectrum licenses unless at least two competing licensees participate in the reverse auction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At least two competing licensees must participate for the Commission to enter such agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice of auction completion and results
rubrics_metrics.description: Public notice shall be provided when the reverse auction is complete and when the forward auction is complete; for the broadcast television spectrum incentive auction, public notice shall be provided of the results of the reverse auction, forward auction, and repacking, and shall indicate that the reassignments and reallocations are effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission will announce completion and results publicly, including repacking and effectiveness of reassignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disbursement of incentive payments — financial information submission
rubrics_metrics.description: A winning bidder shall submit the necessary financial information to facilitate the disbursement of the winning bidder's incentive payment. Specific procedures for submitting financial information, including applicable deadlines, will be set out by public notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Winning bidders must follow public notices for deadlines and procedures to provide bank/financial details for payment disbursement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability and scope for acceptance of gifts to the Commission (Subpart R)
rubrics_metrics.description: This subpart implements procedures governing acceptance of unconditional gifts, donations and bequests to the Commission itself, and applies to travel reimbursement for attendance or participation in government‑sponsored meetings required to carry out the Commission's functions; other employee gifts are governed by government‑wide standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules apply specifically to gifts to the agency (not personal employee gifts) and identify relevant statutory/regulatory cross‑references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'gift' for Commission acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'gift' means any unconditional gift, donation or bequest of real, personal and other property (including voluntary and uncompensated services as authorized under 5 U.S.C. 3109).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the scope of items/services that may be offered as gifts to the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: General prohibitions on solicitation and cash gifts
rubrics_metrics.description: An employee shall not: (1) directly or indirectly solicit or coerce the offering of a gift, donation or bequest to the Commission from a regulated entity or other prohibited source; or (2) accept gifts of cash pursuant to this subpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees must not solicit gifts from regulated entities and may not accept cash gifts under these rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral of gift offers to designated agency ethics official
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who seeks to offer any gift to the Commission shall make such offer to the Commission's designated agency ethics official. Any Commission employee contacted by a potential donor must immediately refer that person to the designated agency ethics official. The designated agency ethics official, in consultation with other agency ethics officials, determines whether acceptance would create a conflict or appearance of conflict and may advise potential donors on types of acceptable equipment/property/services and procedures. The Commission may, in its discretion, afford public notice before accepting any gift.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All offers must pass through the designated ethics official; employees must not engage donors directly and should refer them immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory factors for evaluating conflicts of interest when accepting gifts
rubrics_metrics.description: No gift shall be accepted unless a determination is made that acceptance would not create a conflict of interest or appearance thereof. Designated agency ethics officials shall consider: (a) whether benefits accrue to an individual employee and, if so, whether the employee is responsible for matters affecting the donor and the significance of the employee's role; (b) the nature and sensitivity of any matters pending at the Commission affecting the donor; (c) the timing of the intended gift; (d) the market value of the intended gift; (e) the frequency of other gifts made by the same donor; and (f) the reason underlying the intended gift given in a written statement from the proposed donor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A multi‑factor balancing test is required to determine whether accepting a gift would create a conflict or appearance thereof; documentation of donor's stated reason is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public disclosure recordkeeping for gifts accepted from prohibited sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission's Security Operations Office shall maintain a written record of gifts accepted from prohibited sources pursuant to section 4(g)(3) authority, including: identity of the prohibited source; description of the gift; market value; documentation concerning the prohibited source's reason for the gift as required in § 1.3003(f); a signed statement of verification from the prohibited source that the gift is unconditional and not contingent on any promise or expectation of regulatory benefit; and the date the gift is accepted by the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records must be complete and include verification that the gift is unconditional and not contingent on regulatory favors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semi‑annual reporting of gifts to Congress
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission shall file a semi‑annual report to Congress listing the gift, donor and value of all gifts accepted from any donor under this subpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency must publicly report gifts and values to Congress every six months.
